high.title: In Exactly 15 Days, Vietnamese Securities Market to Receive Important News
high.summary: On August 21, 2026, FTSE Russell will officially announce the list of Vietnamese stocks to be included in the FTSE Global Equity Index Series (FTSE GEIS) under its Emerging Market classification. This precedes the formal upgrade taking effect on September 21, 2026 — a landmark event for Vietnamese capital markets. The upgrade was made possible by Vietnam meeting market accessibility criteria, most notably the rollout of the **Global Broker model**, which allows foreign institutional investors to trade via global brokerages as counterparties. This was supported by **Circular 08/2026/TT-BTC** and improvements to the **Non Pre-Funding (NPF)** mechanism. Under the FTSE Russell roadmap, all Vietnamese stocks will simultaneously be removed from the FTSE Frontier Index in the September 2026 annual review. **Key implications for fund managers:** The August 21 announcement is the next critical catalyst — expect heightened volatility on the VN-Index and significant passive inflow anticipation as global ETFs rebalance. Watch for foreign ownership room constraints and liquidity dynamics on high-weight candidate stocks.

high.title: Vietcap Names 29 Stocks Likely to Attract Billions in USD Inflows Post-Upgrade
high.summary: Vietcap Securities has published a forecast list of **29 Vietnamese stocks** expected to qualify for inclusion in the FTSE GEIS Emerging Market index — notably higher than the 23 stocks previously identified by FTSE Russell. The discrepancy stems from the six-month data lag: FTSE Russell's reference list was based on data as of December 31, 2025, while Vietcap's analysis uses market data updated to **June 30, 2026**. Over this period, material changes in stock prices, free float ratios, foreign ownership room, market capitalization, and liquidity have altered eligibility. The report identifies **4 large-cap stocks** among the 29 qualified names. **For fund managers:** This broader-than-expected inclusion list is bullish for VN-Index sentiment and signals potentially larger passive inflows than the market initially priced. Foreign room availability remains a key constraint to monitor — stocks with limited room may see price premiums but restricted actual foreign buying. The August 21 FTSE announcement will be the definitive moment to reconcile Vietcap's forecast against official inclusion.

high.title: Gold Surpasses $4,300/oz, Experts Forecast New Peak
high.summary: Gold spot prices breached $4,300/oz during the morning session of August 6 (Beijing time), reaching the highest level since June 18. As of 16:00 Vietnam time on August 6, prices had eased slightly to $4,278/oz — still approximately $31/oz above the prior session close. Since July 31, spot gold has surged over 5.8%. The primary driver, according to Guoxin Futures chief analyst Gu Fengda, is a sharp decline in market expectations for further Fed rate hikes. Cooling U.S. labor market data has materially reduced the probability of a September Fed rate increase, simultaneously dragging down both the USD index and U.S. Treasury yields.

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of August 6: Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary: Vietnamese bank deposit rates remain elevated, with the market now showing **8 banks offering 7%/year or above** on 12-month term deposits. ACB leads the market at **7.8%/year** for 12-month terms, also posting 7.6% (6-month) and 7.7% (9-month). LPBank sits second at 7.3% for 12 months. The state-owned "Big 4" — Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, and VietinBank — hold steady at **6.8%/year** for 12- and 18-month terms and 6.6% for 6- and 9-month tenors.

high.title: Vietcap Securities Forecasts VN-Index Could Hit 1,885 Points as Early as August
high.summary:
Following a decline of more than 10% in the first three weeks of July, the VN-Index staged a recovery of nearly 4% in the final stretch of the month, driven by bottom-fishing demand. The rebound was triggered when the VN-Index's trailing P/E ratio — excluding Vingroup stocks — fell below two standard deviations beneath its 10-year median, a valuation extreme previously observed only during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and the corporate bond crisis in late 2022. Technically, Vietcap notes the index successfully formed a base at the 1,665-point support level and has since broken back above its 200-day moving average, now approaching the 50-day moving average near 1,800. Vietcap assigns a 65% base-case probability that the VN-Index reaches 1,885 points within August. For international fund managers, this signals a potential inflection point in Vietnamese equities following a severe correction. The extreme valuation compression and technical recovery suggest renewed buying interest, though persistent foreign selling remains a key headwind to monitor.

---

medium.title: China Announces 20% Tax on Offshore Trust Assets — Ultra-Wealthy Scramble to Comply
medium.summary:
China's Ministry of Finance and State Tax Administration issued sweeping new regulations on July 24 imposing a **20% tax across the full lifecycle of offshore trust structures** — covering establishment, income generation, distribution, and dissolution. Individuals must declare and pay back-taxes on trust assets transferred since early 2023 within a **90-day window ending October 22**, with penalties and interest for late filings. Wealthy Chinese families in Hong Kong and Singapore are reportedly consulting lawyers and considering asset sales to meet the deadline. **Relevance to Vietnam:** This development could accelerate capital flight from China into alternative wealth-management jurisdictions across Southeast Asia, including Vietnam. Hong Kong and Singapore — key feeder markets for Vietnamese real estate and equity investment — may see portfolio reshuffling. Monitor whether this generates incremental capital flows into Vietnamese assets, particularly as Vietnam's EM upgrade simultaneously raises its profile as an investable market.

---

medium.title: Securities Firms Net Sell Over VND 700 Billion in HOSE Shares While Foreign Investors Turn Net Buyers
medium.summary: The VN-Index closed the August 5th session nearly flat, declining just 0.77 points (-0.04%) to 1,776.46 points, amid a mild corrective pullback in the broader market. The most notable flow dynamic of the session was a significant divergence between two key participant groups: proprietary trading desks of securities companies (tự doanh CTCK) were aggressive net sellers, offloading a net VND 728 billion on HOSE, while foreign investors turned net buyers to the tune of VND 478 billion across the whole market. The largest net sell by prop desks was in GEE (VND 285 billion), followed by GAS (VND 77 billion), VPB (VND 51 billion), and VCB (VND 50 billion). Foreign net buying is a marginally positive signal for VND sentiment and broader risk appetite, though the quantum remains modest. The prop desk selling pressure on banking names (VPB, VCB, MBB, LPB) warrants monitoring, as sustained outflows from the financial sector could weigh on the VN-Index near-term. Watch whether foreign net buying continues to provide a floor.

medium.title: Vietcombank Books VND 2,900 Billion Gain Following Full Acquisition of Prime 35-Story Ho Chi Minh City Tower
medium.summary: Vietcombank (VCB), Vietnam's largest listed bank by market capitalization, recorded a VND 2,906 billion surge in other income on its consolidated Q2/2026 financial statements, stemming from a fair value revaluation gain following its acquisition of full (100%) ownership of the Vietcombank Tower joint venture at 5 Me Linh Square, Ho Chi Minh City. Prior to 2026, VCB held 52% of the venture; it subsequently acquired the remaining 48% from partners Setra and Bonday. The total enterprise was valued at approximately VND 6,679 billion based on the transaction price. The VND 564 billion book value of the original 52% stake was revalued upward upon consolidation, generating the one-off accounting gain. For bond and equity investors in VCB, this is a material but non-recurring income item that inflated Q2 headline profit. Investors should strip this out when assessing underlying earnings quality and recurring return on equity. VCB's core lending profitability trends and net interest margin remain the key fundamental drivers to monitor.

medium.title: Vietnam's Major Banks Surpass VND 10,000 Billion Quarterly Profit Milestone — Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, MB, and VPBank Now Each Earn Over VND 10 Trillion Per Quarter
medium.summary: Five of Vietnam's largest banks — Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, MB, and VPBank — each reported pre-tax profits exceeding VND 10 trillion (approximately USD 390 million) in Q2 2026 alone, a threshold that until recently represented a full-year achievement for even the sector's top performers. Vietcombank led the pack with a record-high quarterly profit of VND 17,420 billion, up nearly 58% year-on-year. This robust profitability underscores strong net interest margin expansion, healthy credit growth, and improving asset quality across the sector. For bond and equity investors, this signals systemic banking sector strength, which supports confidence in Vietnamese sovereign credit and reduces near-term concerns about non-performing loan spillovers. High bank profitability also suggests the SBV has room to maintain a stable monetary policy stance without urgency to cut rates further to support bank margins. Watch for whether these earnings translate into increased dividend payouts or capital raises, which could influence equity flows and banking sector weighting in the VN-Index.

medium.title: One Private Bank's Asset Growth Surpasses the Entire Big4 — VPBank's Expansion Equals BIDV and Agribank Combined
medium.summary: As of June 30, 2026, VPBank recorded the largest absolute increase in total assets among 28 surveyed Vietnamese banks in H1 2026, with total assets reaching VND 1,502 trillion — up VND 242,377 billion (+19.2%) versus end-2025, surpassing the combined asset growth of BIDV and Agribank. Vietcombank ranked second with an increase of approximately VND 215 trillion. Only Sacombank and Eximbank saw asset contraction. This rapid balance sheet expansion at private banks signals aggressive credit deployment, which has implications for both monetary conditions (increased broad money supply) and potential SBV macro-prudential responses. For FX traders, accelerating credit growth can be a leading indicator of import demand and domestic inflation pressures, both relevant to VND stability. Bond investors should monitor whether this credit surge is being funded by deposit growth or wholesale borrowing, as the latter could pressure interbank rates and short-end government bond yields.

medium.title: Securities Market Turns Difficult: New Account Openings Drop Sharply
medium.summary:
New domestic securities account openings in July 2026 totaled approximately 227,000 — the second-lowest monthly figure in the past year, exceeded only by February 2026. Cumulatively, domestic investor accounts grew by nearly 1.8 million year-to-date, bringing the total to approximately 13.6 million individual accounts (~13% of the population). However, the headline concern is market performance: the VN-Index fell nearly 7% in July, at one point approaching 1,650 points. Domestic retail money flow stalled while foreign investors sold aggressively, offloading a net VND 11,600 billion (~USD 450 million) on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange during the month. This sustained foreign net selling is a key negative signal for VND capital flows and market sentiment. The combination of foreign outflows, weakening retail participation, and a technically broken VN-Index warrants close monitoring for further downside pressure on equities and potential FX implications if offshore selling accelerates.

---

medium.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of August 4: Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
medium.summary: This August 4 snapshot confirms the same rate structure as the August 6 survey, indicating **rate stability over the short term** with no new movements in the two-day window. ACB continues to lead at 7.8%/year for 12 months, and the Big 4 remain anchored at 6.8%. Notably, the article highlights that **LPBank raised its rates at the start of August** and has maintained those higher levels, suggesting proactive pricing to attract deposits amid tighter liquidity. The consistency across the two surveys reinforces that the current rate environment is entrenched rather than transitory, and that private banks are competing aggressively for retail funding. This is relevant context for modeling Vietnamese government bond yield trajectories and assessing the SBV's likely policy posture heading into Q3 2026.

medium.title: MB Bank Confident in 2026 Profit Plan; Maintains CASA Leadership and Caps Real Estate Loan Ratio at 13% ±2%
HOSE Restricts Margin Trading on 56 Securities in August
medium.summary: The Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HoSE) has published its updated list of securities ineligible for margin trading, which currently stands at 56 tickers as of August 5, 2026. Most affected stocks are under warning, control, restricted, or suspended trading status — including names such as APG, APH, HVN, LDG, OGC, and others. Additional reasons for margin ineligibility include listings under six months old (e.g., AAN, BVB, VBB) and deteriorating financial performance. Two stocks — GHC and TIX — were recently reinstated to the margin-eligible list. While primarily a market microstructure development, the relatively large number of margin-restricted securities reflects ongoing credit quality concerns in the broader equity market and may constrain leveraged trading activity, limiting market liquidity at the margins.

medium.title: A Major Oil & Gas Company Deposits Over VND 42,200 Billion at Banks
medium.summary: PV GAS (HoSE: GAS), Vietnam's state-owned gas corporation, reported Q2/2026 consolidated net revenue of VND 43,249 billion (+43.78% YoY) and post-tax profit of VND 6,021 billion (+25.22% YoY) — the highest quarterly profit in company history. A notable data point is the company's VND 42,200+ billion held in bank deposits, representing a significant injection of corporate liquidity into the Vietnamese banking system. Financial income declined 11.36% YoY to VND 355.9 billion, suggesting lower deposit yields despite the large cash position. **Relevance:** The scale of state-owned enterprise (SOE) deposits at commercial banks is a meaningful variable for domestic liquidity conditions and short-term interbank rates. Large SOE cash holdings parked in the banking system can suppress interbank rates and influence the SBV's open market operations calculus. This is worth monitoring for bond investors tracking the short end of the Vietnamese yield curve.
